task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
within-team variation in lineup role coverage
separability of role coverage from talent and player counts
talent control in lineup-level influence models
methodological_questions: Can lineup role coverage be separated from talent and player-count effects?
Does talent control behave adequately when role coverage is derived from play-by-play possession records?
What confounding, reliability, and outcome-derived label risks threaten a test of lineup role coverage?

historical_evidence.finding: Adaptation quality vs talent as predictor of series wins. Record reports corr(talent, adapt)=+0.124; after talent control, adapt p=0.275 (n~55 series). Its stated failure mechanism is A_unanswerable: a sample of about 55 series could not separate coaching adaptation from roster quality. Limitations recorded: [prior work] and [prior work].

Absence validation. Recorded: 16/23 of V1(a) cases above own-null p95 (binomial p=2.67e-16), and V1(b) mean difference +0.142, CI [+0.103, +0.187] (confirmed). V2a rho=+0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667] (FAIL); V2b partial rho=+0.253, p=0.115 (FAIL). Limitation recorded: [prior work].

Structural concentration vs defensive vulnerability. C1a rho=+0.079, p=0.0882, CI [-0.114, +0.234]; C1b rho=+0.095, p=0.0738; robust 0.2/0.3 variants also fail. Recorded as B_powered_null on n=117, 30 franchises, with the CI spanning 0. Limitation recorded: [prior work].

Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type. Reported lineup-cell PPP gaps (e.g., Jokic vs MIN 0.814, n=59; Giannis forced PULL_UP 0.848 vs preferred DRIVE) with no placebo or matching. Record states later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. Failure mechanism recorded as E_unclear; validation status NOT_RECORDED.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Estimating a talent-adjusted effect of a coaching/structural-style variable on outcomes at series level
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable. After talent control the adaptation term was not significant (p=0.275) and [prior work] states that the sample of about 55 series could not separate the coaching variable from roster quality. Talent and the target variable were correlated (+0.124).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading lineup-by-play-type PPP gaps as evidence of structural suppression without placebo or matching
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear with no placebo or matching, and later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts. Lineup cells were small (n about 30 to 59). [prior work] is not a hypothesis test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting a team-level structural concentration effect on an outcome with about 30 franchises
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as B_powered_null, but [prior work] also lists [prior work]. The CI spans 0, so the study cannot distinguish a small effect from none at this sample size.

evidence_establishes: Across the retrieved records, talent-adjusted tests of structural or coaching-style variables on outcomes have repeatedly been underpowered or unresolved, with the same confounding and small-sample limitations recorded (SF-[prior work], SF-[prior work], [prior work]).
Unadjusted lineup-cell gaps built from play-by-play graphs were not treated as valid evidence without placebo or matching (SF-[prior work]).
The retrieved records give a prior sense of what a null or untestable result looks like on this kind of data, which helps set expectations for power and design.
evidence_does_not_establish: None of the retrieved records studies lineup coverage of organizer, shaper, or terminal roles. No role definitions, coverage measure, or separability test for these roles were returned.
No record reports within-team variation in lineup role coverage, or whether coverage is separable from talent and player counts in this dataset.
No record shows whether talent control behaves for the 2022-23 to 2025-26 NBA data at lineup or possession level.
The retrieved records do not state the exact sample sizes or effect sizes for the present question, and they do not validate the derived play-type possession records.
own_inferences: The question bundles three claims (within-team coverage variation, separability from talent and counts, and talent-control behaviour). Each needs its own test, and the separability claim is the one most at risk.

With 90 team-seasons and within-team variation, coverage may be partly collinear with roster composition and player count, so the separability claim could fail for reasons unrelated to any real role effect.
The organizer, shaper, and terminal roles are not defined in any retrieved record. Their definitions would need to be fixed before analysis, or results would depend on undisclosed choices.
Talent measured from regular-season net rating would be partly outcome-derived for regular-season outcomes, which invites circularity in talent control.
uncertainties: Role definitions and the coverage measure are not provided in the task statement or the retrieved records.
The talent measure to be used is not specified, and whether it is independent of the outcome is unknown.
Whether 2025-26 playoff possession records are reliable enough for inclusion is unknown; they are complete only from 2026-06-21, which is before the 2026-07-13 date.
Reliability of role labels derived from the play-by-play is unknown.
The retrieval returned no record that directly addresses this question, so prior-work coverage may be incomplete.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records are about related but different questions. They do not answer lineup role coverage. They still changed the design: SF-[prior work] and SF-[prior work] showed that talent-adjusted and lineup-cell analyses fail without an independent talent measure, placebo tests, or matching, and SF-[prior work] showed that the sample size needs a power calculation first. These shaped the proceed_with_changes decision and the design below. They did not establish an answer to the question.

blocking_constraints.text: Role coverage is likely correlated with talent and roster composition, as in SF-[prior work], so the separability claim can fail even if the roles matter.
With 90 team-seasons and within-team variation, power for a small coverage effect is likely limited, as in SF-[prior work].
Talent measures built from the same regular-season net rating as the outcome would make talent control circular.
Role labels derived from play-by-play may be unreliable, and their reliability is not established in any retrieved record.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record addresses lineup coverage of organizer, shaper, or terminal roles. The cited records are on related questions: adaptation vs talent (untestable), absence validation (partly confirmed, with the V2 tests failing), structural concentration vs defensive vulnerability (rejected as a powered null), and superstar suppression by lineup (not a hypothesis test, treated as artifact-prone). They inform risks and design but do not answer the question.

risks.text: Talent and roster composition may drive both coverage and outcome, so the separability claim may be confounded; SF-[prior work] was untestable for this reason.
90 team-seasons may give too little power for within-team coverage effects; SF-[prior work] was a powered-looking null with a CI spanning 0.
If talent is measured from the same net rating as the outcome, talent control is circular.
Role labels from play-by-play may be unstable across games and seasons; no reliability check exists in the retrieved records.
Some lineups or role combinations will have few possessions, as in the small lineup cells of SF-[prior work] (n about 30 to 59).
Without placebo role assignments, any coverage effect may reflect lineup composition rather than role; SF-[prior work] was flagged for this.
Three roles, several coverage definitions, and several talent controls create many possible tests; SF-[prior work] shows the risk of selecting among cells.
Play-type and initiator labels from the derived graph may be mislabelled, so role assignments may be wrong.
Roles and play styles change across 2022-23 to 2025-26, so pooling seasons may mix different regimes.

design.estimand: Within team-season, the partial association between lineup-level role coverage (at least one organizer, shaper, or terminal on court) and lineup net points per 100 possessions, conditional on a pre-specified out-of-sample talent measure and player count, together with a separability diagnostic showing coverage is not collinear with talent or count.
design.unit: Lineup-stint (lineup of five on court during a continuous interval), nested in team-season.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 (complete from 2026-04-13). Playoffs are excluded from the primary test and used only as a pre-registered sensitivity analysis. Target 90 team-seasons; exclude lineups below a pre-set possession minimum.
design.power: Compute power before running: simulate a coverage effect of a pre-specified minimum effect size at 90 team-seasons with cluster-robust variance. Proceed only if power at the minimum effect size is adequate; otherwise report the test as underpowered and do not claim a null.
design.controls: Talent from an out-of-sample source (prior season or independent rating), not the outcome season's net rating. Team-season fixed effects, minutes-weighted player count, and lineup-level shrinkage. Report VIF or partial-correlation diagnostics between coverage and talent/count. Role definitions fixed in writing before analysis.
design.falsification: Placebo role assignment: shuffle role labels across players within team-season and confirm the coverage effect disappears. Negative-control outcome (e.g., defensive rebounds) should show no coverage effect. Pre-register a separability failure (coverage explained by talent with R-squared above a set threshold) as an outcome that blocks the claim.
design.multiplicity: One primary test (organizer-or-shaper-or-terminal coverage, out-of-sample talent control). Role-specific tests, alternative talent measures, and playoff analyses are secondary and labelled exploratory. Apply Holm correction across the secondary family.
design.decision_rule: Claim within-team coverage variation and separability only if the separability diagnostic passes and the primary coverage effect CI excludes 0 after talent control and placebo checks pass. If the separability diagnostic fails, report the question as untestable with this data. If the CI spans 0 at adequate power, report a powered null. Otherwise report inconclusive.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 full seasons and 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) from the per-game NBA stats API files, plus derived play-type possession records as of 2026-07-13. 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21) used only in sensitivity analysis. Freeze the data snapshot and role definitions before analysis.
